panels.description: Each row is one link or node over time. Gateway link queries combine exporter pod identities so replacements do not add rows; overlapping reports show Down if either reports Down. A blank stretch means Mimir has no samples for it: home was unreachable and the data was not (or not yet) replayed from a home buffer. The OVH-side Ready rows go Down during an outage; the rows scraped at home show what home itself saw once their buffer is replayed.
panels.title: Home connectivity timeline

panels.description: Traffic through the gateway's WAN port. Traffic scale selects linear or base-10 symlog; the log view remains linear below 1 bit/s so zero stays visible.
panels.title: Internet throughput (gateway WAN)

panels.description: Actual negotiated Ethernet speed between CRS310 ether1 and the AT&T BGW320 gateway, sampled every 30 seconds. Compare its transitions with the independent host ping-loss panels beside it.

panels.description: Share of pings from optiplex (5/s per target) that got no reply. Loss to the gateway with none to the switch is the uplink fault in debug/home_network_connectivity/2026_10_gateway_uplink_loss.md.
panels.title: Ping loss from optiplex

panels.description: ICMP probes from wyrm2 to the AT&T gateway, MikroTik switch, optiplex LAN address (192.168.1.10), and ovh-ns104952 over Nebula. Loss is the unanswered fraction of 5 pings/s, averaged over 5 minutes. Compare with optiplex beside it; a gap means missing observations.
panels.title: Ping loss from wyrm2

panels.description: Mean round-trip time of answered pings from optiplex, per target.
panels.title: Ping RTT from optiplex

panels.description: ICMP probes from wyrm2 to the AT&T gateway, MikroTik switch, optiplex LAN address (192.168.1.10), and ovh-ns104952 over Nebula. Mean round-trip time of answered pings, per target.
panels.title: Ping RTT from wyrm2

panels.description: UNRELIABLE: captures at OptiPlex found invalid ICMP checksums in Netwatch requests; reported loss matched the malformed requests, and enabling a concurrent probe changed the pattern. These measurements cannot establish network delivery or outage frequency. Use the independent OptiPlex and wyrm2 host probes for reliability. Latest reported Netwatch batch, sent by the CRS310 itself: 200 pings at 150 ms intervals once per minute, with a 1 s reply timeout and no early termination. Unlike host smokeping, this is batch loss, not a rolling 5-minute ratio. Scraped every 30 seconds; gaps cannot reconstruct missed batches.
panels.title: UNRELIABLE: Ping batch loss from MikroTik

panels.description: UNRELIABLE: captures at OptiPlex found invalid ICMP checksums in Netwatch requests; reported loss matched the malformed requests, and enabling a concurrent probe changed the pattern. These measurements cannot establish network delivery or outage frequency. Use the independent OptiPlex and wyrm2 host probes for reliability. Mean RTT of answered pings in the latest reported switch-originated Netwatch batch. 200 pings at 150 ms intervals, once per minute; scraped every 30 seconds. A zero RTT during 100% loss does not mean a fast response.
panels.title: UNRELIABLE: Ping batch RTT from MikroTik

panels.description: UNRELIABLE: captures at OptiPlex found invalid ICMP checksums in Netwatch requests; reported loss matched the malformed requests, and enabling a concurrent probe changed the pattern. These measurements cannot establish network delivery or outage frequency. Use the independent OptiPlex and wyrm2 host probes for reliability. Estimated failed batches in the trailing hour, from reset-aware increase of RouterOS cumulative failed-tests (exported as a gauge by mktxp). Each batch tests 200 pings once per minute; a 5% loss threshold and 1 s RTT thresholds determine failure. This measures failed batches, not distinct outage episodes. Counts can survive missed scrapes unless a probe resets; increase may produce fractional estimates.
panels.title: UNRELIABLE: Failed probe batches per hour from MikroTik

panels.description: Number of one-minute classifications with at least 1% unanswered host ICMP pings. This is measured affected time, up to 60 minutes per hour, per source and target. A minute is classified only with fresh, reset-free request and reply counters and roughly 5 requests/s. Missing observations are excluded; compare the coverage panel. Computed from raw probe samples when queried, so buffered samples can fill historical gaps after delivery.
panels.title: Affected probe minutes per trailing hour

panels.description: An episode starts when an observed healthy minute (under 1% loss) is followed immediately by an affected minute (at least 1% loss). A return from a telemetry gap is left-censored and does not start a new counted episode. Zero requires at least one observed minute. Computed from raw probe samples when queried, so buffered samples can fill historical gaps after delivery.
panels.title: Observed episode starts per trailing hour
